title: The Role of Dominant Lesion Site and SUVmax in the Depth of PSA Response in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Depth of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response is prognostic in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), and the SUVmax of the most avid lesion is a readily available parameter on staging PSMA PET/CT. Uptake intensity and the anatomical site of that lesion are, however, distinct features. This study evaluated their associations with the depth of PSA response. Methods: In this retrospective single-centre study of men receiving androgen deprivation therapy plus an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI), the SUVmax and anatomical site of the dominant lesion were derived from baseline 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT. The primary outcome was a PSA nadir < 0.2 ng/mL, analysed using logistic regression with sequential adjustment and within strata defined by disease burden. Progression-free survival (PFS) was a secondary outcome. Results: Among 100 men with evaluable baseline PET/CT, SUVmax was associated with neither PSA response depth nor PFS in any parameterisation examined. A deep PSA response was achieved by 72%, 52% and 29% of patients with prostate-, node- and bone-dominant disease (trend p < 0.001), with median nadirs of 0.08, 0.19 and 0.50 ng/mL. Among patients with bone metastases, a deep response occurred in 29% with bone-dominant disease and 57% with a dominant lesion elsewhere (p = 0.016). The association persisted across sequentially adjusted models (OR range 0.22-0.33) and within high-volume disease (p = 0.008). Under a six-month landmark, deep PSA response was associated with longer PFS (HR 0.10, 95% CI 0.01-0.42), whereas bone dominance was not. Conclusions: The site of the dominant PSMA PET/CT lesion, but not its SUVmax, was associated with the depth of PSA response in ARPI-treated mHSPC. These findings require prospective validation.

title: Clinical Utility of 18F-FDG PET/CT for Staging and Restaging of Pediatric Malignant Melanoma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Malignant melanoma is a rare entity in the pediatric population, accounting for approximately 1-3% of all childhood malignancies. Despite its rarity, it is the most common skin cancer in children. Accurate staging and monitoring are essential for treatment planning and prognosis. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical value of 18F-FDG PET/CT in staging and restaging of pediatric malignant melanoma. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed pediatric patients aged 18 years or younger who underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging between 2010 and 2025 with histopathologically confirmed malignant melanoma. Demographic data, primary lesion localization, PET/CT findings, pathology reports, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Lesions were categorized as positive and negative in the final analysis. Diagnostic performance parameters (with 95% confidence intervals (CIs)) were calculated using histopathological confirmation or clinical follow-up as the reference standard, and categorical associations were assessed using Fisher's exact test. Results: A total of 20 patients (12 females, 8 males; mean age: 11 years, range: 4-18) and 31 PET/CT examinations were included, with a mean follow-up duration of approximately 98 months. PET/CT was performed for initial staging in 17 examinations and for restaging in 14. On an examination-based analysis, PET/CT findings were negative in 22/31 (71.0%) and positive in 9/31 (29.0%) examinations. On a patient-based analysis, 12/20 (60%) patients had all examinations classified as true negative and remained disease-free throughout follow-up. 18F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated a sensitivity of 80.0% (95% CI: 49.0-94.3%), specificity of 95.2% (95% CI: 77.3-99.2%), positive predictive value of 88.9% (95% CI: 56.5-98.0%), negative predictive value of 90.9% (95% CI: 72.2-97.5%), and overall accuracy of 90.3% (95% CI: 75.1-96.7%) for the detection of clinically active disease. Agreement between PET/CT findings and clinical outcomes was substantial (Cohen's κ = 0.77). Among the nine PET-negative restaging examinations, one was subsequently confirmed as false-negative; the remaining eight showed no evidence of active disease during the available follow-up period. title: An Overview of Cushing's Syndrome Caused by Ectopic Adrenocorticotropin Secretion.
abstract: Ectopic Cushing's syndrome (ECS) causes 10% to 20% of all cases of endogenous hypercortisolism. It is caused by the aberrant secretion of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) or corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) due to the presence of an ectopic tumor. The latter is usually a neuroendocrine (NEN) tumor (mostly thoracic NENs such as bronchial NEN neoplasms, thymic NEN neoplasms, small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC), or pancreatic NEN neoplasms). Clinical presentation is heterogeneous: an aggressive phenotype, typically driven by rapidly growing, poorly differentiated tumors such as small-cell lung carcinoma, manifests with severe symptoms of acute onset, predominant myopathy, resistant arterial hypertension, hypokalemia, and severe hyperpigmentation, usually without the centripetal obesity typical of Cushing's syndrome; conversely, an indolent phenotype, more often related to well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms such as bronchial carcinoids, may present with the classic centripetal fat distribution, facial plethora, and purple striae also seen in Cushing's disease, making clinical distinction between the two difficult. The diagnosis of ECS can be cumbersome and time-consuming. Once hypercortisolism is confirmed, the most critical step is to distinguish patients with an ectopic source of ACTH from those with pituitary adenoma. Dynamic endocrine tests such as the high-dose dexamethasone suppression test, CRH stimulation tests, desmopressin tests, and bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling (BIPSS) can be helpful in the differential diagnosis. BIPSS is considered the gold standard for distinguishing a pituitary from a non-pituitary source of ACTH: the absence of a central-to-peripheral ACTH gradient supports, but does not by itself localize or confirm, an ectopic source. Tumor localization is achieved by a multimodality imaging protocol, including initial high-resolution computed tomography (CT) scans, followed by functional imaging, mainly Gallium-68-labeled somatostatin receptor positron emission tomography (PET)/CT scans. However, in 10-20% of these patients, the tumors cannot be localized. The treatment of ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism is two-fold: one is to immediately control hypercortisolism to prevent life-threatening complications (opportunistic infections and thromboembolism), and the second is to definitively treat the tumor. title: Multimodal Evaluation of [225Ac]Ac-PSMA-617 Therapy in mCRPC: PET Based Total Tumor Volume, PSA Kinetics, and Blood Biomarkers.
mesh: Humans; Male; Prostate-Specific Antigen; Prostatic Neoplasms, Castration-Resistant; Dipeptides; Heterocyclic Compounds, 1-Ring; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Biomarkers, Tumor; Tumor Burden; Aged; Middle Aged; Retrospective Studies; Radiopharmaceuticals; Actinium; Kinetics
abstract: This retrospective analysis interrogates the value of a multimodal biomarker paradigm to characterize molecular and clinical responses to [225Ac]Ac-PSMA-617-targeted α-therapy (TAT) in cohorts of heavily pretreated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who had shown limited benefit from prior [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. By integrating quantitative PSMA-PET/CT metrics-notably total tumor volume (TTV) and lesion SUV indices-with longitudinal PSA kinetics, routine hematologic and biochemical markers, and semiquantitative assessment of salivary gland uptake, we sought to delineate treatment effect, organ-specific off-target impact, and prognostic biomarker signatures. In twelve patients receiving 2-6 cycles of therapy (median activity 8 MBq), biochemical responses were frequent: 8/12 experienced PSA declines and 5/12 achieved ≥50% reduction. Concordant molecular responses were observed on PSMA-PET, with SUVpeak-based partial response in 7/12, stable disease in 3/12, and progressive disease in 2/12 of the target lesions. Qualitative concordance between TTV and PSA response was observed in four illustrative patients; no formal cohort-level concordance analysis was performed. Notably, salivary gland tracer uptake on [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT decreased after two cycles of [225Ac]Ac-PSMA-617 compared with baseline (SUVmax -63.7%; SUVmean -45.5%). In this exploratory cohort, elevations in PSA, alkaline phosphatase, and LDH measured after two cycles of therapy, along with low hemoglobin, platelet count, and creatinine, were associated with shorter overall survival. Median progression-free survival and overall survival were 27 and 53 weeks, respectively. Collectively, these findings suggest that a combined PSMA-PET TTV-PSA-blood biomarker framework may offer complementary insight alongside PSA alone for characterizing therapeutic response, although its incremental value over PSA was not formally tested in this exploratory cohort; blood-based biomarkers (PSA, ALP) showed the most consistent prognostic association with survival, providing objective measures of both tumor response and collateral tissue impact. Prospective validation in larger, controlled cohorts is warranted to refine biomarker thresholds and guide personalized TAT strategies.

title: Early Dynamic 18F-FDG PET/CT SUVmax and Its Association with Pathological Stage and Tumor Grade in Bladder Cancer: A Prospective Exploratory Study.
mesh: Humans; Male; Female; Prospective Studies; Fluorodeoxyglucose F18; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Urinary Bladder Neoplasms; Middle Aged; Aged; Neoplasm Staging; Neoplasm Grading; ROC Curve; Radiopharmaceuticals
abstract: Background and Objectives: Accurate preoperative staging and grade assessment are crucial for optimal treatment selection in bladder cancer. This prospective study evaluated multi-timepoint Fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging for predicting pathological stage and tumor grade. Materials and Methods: Seventy-two patients with bladder carcinoma underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT including early dynamic (0-2, 2-4, 8-10 min), standard (60 min), and late (~120 min) imaging following a standardized furosemide hydration protocol. Maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were correlated with histopathological findings. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis with Youden index for optimal cut-offs. Results: The cohort comprised 72 patients (84.7% male, mean age 64.8 ± 10.7 years) with pathological stages Ta (36.1%), CIS (15.3%), T1 (31.9%), and T2 (16.7%). High-grade tumors demonstrated significantly higher SUVmax at early dynamic imaging (0-2 min: 1.50 vs. 1.00, p = 0.028) and late imaging (11.40 vs. 9.50, p = 0.045) compared to low-grade tumors. Early dynamic imaging at 0-2 min achieved the highest, although modest, diagnostic performance for high-grade prediction (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.652) and muscle-invasive disease prediction (AUC = 0.669), with optimal cut-offs of SUVmax = 1.40 and 1.80, respectively. Early dynamic SUVmax correlated significantly with tumor grade (ρ = 0.261, p = 0.027) and tumor size (ρ = 0.424, p < 0.001). The negative predictive value for muscle-invasive disease was 90.4%, but sensitivity was only 58.3%. Conclusions: Early dynamic 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging at 0-2 min showed the highest, although modest, diagnostic performance among the evaluated time points for predicting tumor grade and muscle invasion. The identified SUVmax cut-offs are exploratory and require external validation in larger multicenter studies before clinical use. Trial registration: Not registered.

title: Ionic-Liquid-Catalyzed Depolymerization of PET: BHET Recovery and Re-Polymerization.
abstract: The accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste presents significant environmental challenges due to its extensive usage and low global recycling rates. Among the available recycling routes, chemical depolymerization by glycolysis offers a promising way to recover high-value monomers. In this study, six ionic liquids (ILs) were tested as homogeneous catalysts for the glycolysis of post-consumer PET bottles in ethylene glycol (EG) at 200 °C for 3 h, alongside an uncatalyzed control. 1-Butyl-3-methylimidazolium acetate ([BMIM][OAc]) and trihexyltetradecylphosphonium decanoate ([P6,6,6,14][Dec]) gave complete PET conversion with isolated bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) yields of 33.6% and 72.4%, respectively. Moreover, trihexyltetradecylphosphonium bis(2,4,4-trimethylpentyl)phosphinate ([P6,6,6,14][TMPP]) reached 56% conversion with no separable product; however, the other three chloride-based ILs and the control reaction demonstrated negligible conversion at the given process parameters. The recovered BHET was characterized by FT-IR, 1H and 13C NMR and GC-MS, and further, was re-polymerized by melt polycondensation at 270 °C. The FT-IR fingerprint, thermogravimetric decomposition profile and solid-state 13C NMR spectrum indicated that the properties of the recycled PET compete with those of the bottlegrade PET. Their melting peak lay 7.7 °C below the reference on first heating (240.6 vs. 248.3 °C) but rose to 248.5 °C on second heating, 3.3 °C above the reference, suggesting that the initial difference arises mainly from crystal perfection and thermal history rather than from an altered chain structure.

title: Rational Design of Molecularly Imprinted Nanozymes for Selective Degradation of Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC).
abstract: Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC) is an engineering thermoplastic whose recycling is hindered by its Code-7 classification and environmental BPA leaching. Here, we report water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes for the selective depolymerization of BPA-PC under mild alkaline conditions. Synthesized within cross-linked surfactant micelles, the optimized nanozyme combines shape-complementary BPA-matched pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. Fluorescence titrations with a soluble dansyl-labeled BPA-PC dimer confirm strong substrate recognition (Ka ~106 M-1). Gel permeation chromatography reveals uniform reductions of 52-55% across Mn, Mw, and Mz, indicative of a random endo-chain cleavage mechanism. On macroscopic BPA-PC films, the nanozyme induces pronounced cracking and surface erosion, whereas polyethylene terephthalate (PET) control films remain undamaged. Furthermore, the aqueous nanozyme retains ~75% of its initial catalytic activity across five consecutive degradation cycles following simple phase extraction. This study demonstrates that tailored, shape-complementary nanozymes provide a generalizable, selective biocatalytic alternative for the circular chemical recycling of recalcitrant engineering plastics.

title: Single-Stage PET Waste Upcycling into Copolymers: Study of Thermal Properties and Crystallization.
abstract: The transesterification of polyester with hydroxyl-terminated oligoesters represents a promising route for the chemical upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate waste. The single-stage melt process under investigation yielded value-added PET-based copolyesters containing up to 15 mol.% diethylene glycol and triethylene glycol units. The effect of comonomer content on the thermal properties and crystallization of the copolymers was studied. It was found that an increase in the number of oxyethylene groups in the comonomer leads to a greater decrease in the glass transition temperature and the isothermal crystallization rate. Diethylene glycol was shown to lower the equilibrium melting temperature more than triethylene glycol. Thus, during PET upcycling, the glass transition temperature decreased from 80 to 50 °C, and the melting temperature from 280 to 250 °C.

title: Characterizing bone metastases and skeletal-related events in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms utilizing 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography.
mesh: Humans; Neuroendocrine Tumors; Female; Bone Neoplasms; Organometallic Compounds; Male; Middle Aged; Retrospective Studies; Aged; Positron-Emission Tomography; Adult; Fractures, Bone; Aged, 80 and over
abstract: Tumors of neuroendocrine origin are a heterogenous group of related neoplasms which can arise from anywhere in the body. Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are categorized by site of origin, differentiation status and grade (Ki-67 expression and/or mitotic rate), with significant prognostic variability accordingly. Historically, the prevalence of bone metastasis is reported to be 6%-12% based on "first generation" (i.e., 111Indium pentetreotide [Octreoscan®]) somatostatin receptor imaging (SSRI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study including patients with well-differentiated NENs to determine the clinical and imaging characteristics of osseous metastases when evaluated with higher-sensitivity 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scans, as well as determining fracture prevalence in selected sub-cohorts. We also developed a risk score analysis to assess risk of fracture in this cohort. Four hundred twenty-four patients were identified for inclusion. The median age was 61 years. Most patients were asymptomatic (64%), had sclerotic lesions (77%), Krenning 4 (71%), and had >3 sites (69%) of osseous disease. A high proportion of patients had osseous metastases at sites with high risk for fracture, including vertebra (82%), pelvis (63%), and peri-trochanteric femur (34%). Fifty-seven patients (13%) in the entire cohort suffered a fracture. Fracture prevalence was significantly lower in small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs, 7%) and Grades 1 and 2 disease (8% and 9%, respectively), with higher prevalence in pancreatic NETs, paragangliomas/pheochromocytomas, lung carcinoid, and Grade 3 disease (≥20% for each; p-values <.05). Our study showed that the rate of osseous metastatic disease approximates 20% in well-differentiated NENs. Most bone metastases are asymptomatic and the risk of fracture is variable based on the primary site of disease and tumor grade. Our novel risk score analysis for fracture was designed to assist clinician decision making as to management of bone metastasis in this patient population.

title: Aggregation-Induced Photodegradable and Hydrolyzable Photosensitizer for Cu64 Positron Emission Tomography/Photoacoustic Imaging-Guided Phototherapy Nanoplatforms with Controllable Performance.
abstract: Radio imaging and optical imaging offer complementary advantages for biomedical diagnosis. However, the photosensitizers used in imaging must be degraded to reduce phototoxicity during phototherapy. Herein, we report a novel dicyanomethylene-based near-infrared photosensitizer (PS) that self-degrades via multiple pathways, including hydrolysis, aggregation-induced photodegradation, and oxidation by hypochlorous acid. To meet diverse theranostic requirements, the degradation behavior and performance of the PS were systematically regulated through co-assembly with three carriers. First, co-assembly with DSPE-PEG2000 produced a nanosystem that is stable to laser irradiation and water during multimodal diagnosis, and labeling with 64Cu enabled dual-mode photoacoustic and radio signal imaging. Second, co-assembly with PLGA-PEG5000 reduced the photodegradation rate by enabling complete degradation through hydrolysis, thereby facilitating deep-tumor phototherapy. Third, complexation with cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) selectively inhibited the hydrolytic properties of the photosensitizer, thereby reducing its phototoxicity through photodegradation and oxidative degradation pathways when superficial tumors are subjected to phototherapy. The phototherapeutic efficacy of the designed nanosystems was validated in a subcutaneous 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model. The results demonstrated effective tumor inhibition with minimal phototoxicity, confirming the suitability of the developed system for safe phototherapy. Overall, this work presents a rational strategy for tuning photosensitizer degradation pathways to balance imaging performance, therapeutic efficacy, and biosafety, providing a versatile platform for multimodal theranostic applications.

title: 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Detection of Locoregional Lymph Node Metastases in Gynecologic Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
mesh: Humans; Female; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Lymphatic Metastasis; Carcinoma, Squamous Cell; Aged; Middle Aged; Aged, 80 and over; Retrospective Studies; Adult; Gallium Radioisotopes; Lymph Nodes; Genital Neoplasms, Female; Radiopharmaceuticals; Quinolines
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Detection of locoregional lymph node (LN) metastases is a critical prognostic factor in gynecologic squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is limited by insufficient specificity, potentially leading to overtreatment. We evaluated gallium-68 fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (68Ga-FAPI-04) positron-emission tomography (PET)/CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in this setting, using CT as comparator. PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT scans of 15 patients with gynecologic SCC (nine cervical, six vulvar carcinomas; mean age 56.3 years, range=38-86 years) were analyzed. PET/CT and CT were read independently by two blinded readers. Histopathology and/or clinical and radiological follow-up (12-18 months) served as the reference standard. Diagnostic performance was calculated on a patient-based level; maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmax) were compared using Welch's t-test and the Mann-Whitney U-test. RESULTS: Histopathological confirmation was available in 12 patients; three were classified by follow-up. LN metastases were confirmed in five patients. 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT achieved a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV) and accuracy of 100%. CT achieved a sensitivity and NPV of 100% but produced false-positive findings in three patients (specificity=70%, PPV=62.5%, accuracy=80%), caused by tattoo-associated lymphadenopathy, sarcoidosis and reactive nodal enlargement, none of which showed pathological tracer uptake. Metastatic LNs exhibited higher SUVmax (mean 23.2±6.0) than nodes false-positive on CT (mean 4.5±4.6; p=0.004 and p=0.036). Primary tumors were visualized in all patients undergoing initial staging; peritoneal nodules down to 7 mm were detected. CONCLUSION: In this small cohort, 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT showed a higher observed specificity than contrast-enhanced CT for the detection of locoregional LN metastases in gynecologic SCC, with no false-negative cases observed.

title: Unusual [18F]FDOPA PET-CT maging of insulinomas in children.
abstract: PURPOSE: Insulinomas are rare pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, causing recurrent episodes of hypoglycaemia. Accurate localisation is essential for surgical management, yet imaging remains challenging. This case series presents unusual findings of paediatric insulinomas on [18F]-dihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]FDOPA) positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) imaging. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed medical notes and investigations of histologically proven paediatric insulinoma cases (n=4) presenting to Royal Manchester Children's Hospital between 2008 and 2024. All patients underwent [18F]FDOPA PET-CT as part of their diagnostic workup. Imaging findings were analysed, with particular attention to tracer uptake patterns. RESULTS: Contrary to the increased tracer uptake typically seen in neuroendocrine tumours, three of the four insulinomas demonstrated focal photopenia at the site of the tumour on [18F]FDOPA PET-CT. Only one case showed increased uptake, suggesting a predominance of reduced, rather than enhanced, tracer activity in paediatric insulinomas CONCLUSION: Photopenia on [18F]FDOPA PET-CT may be a more frequent finding than increased uptake in paediatric insulinomas. Recognizing this atypical pattern is important for accurate tumour localisation before surgical management. Further studies are needed to validate these findings and find a mechanistic explanation.

title: Orbital involvement by spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma: a case report of a rare and aggressive tumor with diagnostic challenges.
mesh: Humans; Female; Middle Aged; Carcinoma, Squamous Cell; Orbital Neoplasms; Magnetic Resonance Imaging; Diagnosis, Differential; Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography
abstract: BACKGROUND: Spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma (SCSCC) is a rare and poorly differentiated variant of squamous cell carcinoma that may mimic sarcoma, melanoma, and other spindle cell malignancies. Orbital involvement is exceptionally uncommon and may pose substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when overt squamous differentiation is absent. CASE PRESENTATION: A 60-year-old woman with a history of left ocular evisceration for a blind painful eye presented six months later with rapidly progressive painful swelling of the left lower eyelid and medial canthus. Orbital magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an infiltrative, heterogeneously enhancing orbital mass, and positron emission tomography-computed tomography showed hypermetabolic uptake in the orbital lesion with additional ipsilateral cervical and parotid-region foci. The patient underwent orbital exenteration combined with radical neck dissection and radical parotidectomy. Histopathologic examination revealed a malignant spindle cell neoplasm with marked pleomorphism and frequent mitotic activity, without definite keratinization or overt squamous differentiation. Immunohistochemical staining showed strong positivity for pancytokeratin AE1/AE3, CK OSCAR, and CK8/18, supporting epithelial differentiation and a diagnosis most consistent with spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma. Despite adjuvant radiotherapy and systemic chemotherapy, metastatic disease developed within three months, and the patient died six months after orbital exenteration. CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty and aggressive clinical behavior of orbital spindle cell malignancies with features most consistent with spindle cell squamous cell carcinoma. Broad immunohistochemical evaluation, careful clinicopathological correlation, comprehensive staging, and early multidisciplinary management are essential in such rare and high-risk tumors.

title: Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology of a Postoperative Foreign Body Reaction Mimicking Peritoneal Metastasis From Colon Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) is a very useful tool in the management of oncological patients. It is a straightforward and quick diagnostic tool, and it can also obtain material for molecular studies that can help guide therapy. However, FNAC is not always performed when radiological studies seem conclusive. We herein report a peculiar case in which FNAC diagnosis completely changed the management of a patient. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A 75-year-old man underwent laparoscopic surgical resection of TNM stage I low-grade intestinal adenocarcinoma. A follow-up CT scan 1 year after surgery revealed multiple peritoneal nodules in the left flank, with an increased FDG uptake in the PET-CT. Radiological diagnosis was peritoneal seeding of carcinoma. FNAC was performed to confirm diagnosis, obtaining a blue material. The smears revealed a large number of histocytes engulfing a dark blue material with no tumour cells. Radiological follow-up was decided and 2 and a half years after diagnosis, the nodules have remained stable and the FDG uptake has steadily decreased over time. DISCUSSION: Foreign-body reaction against sutures and meshes employed in abdominal surgery has been widely analysed in experimental models. Lymphocytes and histiocytes are the main inflammatory cells responsible for this reaction. In the literature there are few reports of foreign-body reaction mimicking peritoneal seeding of carcinomas, and all of them were diagnosed with a biopsy of suspicious nodules. A thorough review of the literature has not revealed any similar case in which FNAC allowed diagnosis of foreign body reaction avoiding the need of surgical exploration and unnecessary systemic therapy. CONCLUSION: We herein report a unique case in which FNAC led to the correct diagnosis of a foreign body reaction, avoiding aggressive measures in an oncologic patient.

title: Unveiling the heterogeneity: PD-L1 expression and metabolic activity in primary vs. metastatic NSCLC, a retrospective single-center analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression was different in primary tumors (PT) and metastatic tumors (MT). Total-body positron-emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) comprehensively visualizes primary lesions and metastases. We aimed to explore the heterogeneity of PD-L1 high expression and metabolic activity between primary and metastatic lesions in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS: Immunohistochemistry analysis (IHC) was conducted for PD-L1 expression on tumor cells (TC) and tumor-infiltrating immune cells (IC) with 22C3 antibody. PD-L1 positive scores on TC no less than 50% or IC no less than 10% was defined as high expression. Total 598 (456 adenocarcinoma (ADC) and 142 squamous cell lung carcinoma (SCC)) primary diagnosed NSCLC patients who underwent 18F-FDG-PET/CT imaging were collected retrospectively. The statistic methods included chi-square test, Mann Whitney test and multivariate regression. RESULTS: 598 patients included 441 with PD-L1 low expression and 157 high expression. In all subtypes and ADC, MT had higher PD-L1 high expression (P = 0.023 and P = 0.010, respectively). The maximum standard uptake value (SUVmax) of PD-L1 high expression was significantly higher than that of PD-L1 low expression, no matter in PT or MT (15.23 (8.85) vs 9.42 (8.34), P<0.001; 13.36 (5.55) vs 8.52 (6.93), P<0.001). The squamous-cell-carcinoma metastatic-lesion analyses were exploratory owing to the very small sample size and risk of type-II statistical error. Multivariate regression indicated that SUVmax was independently associated with PD-L1 high expression. In all metastatic sites, we compared the SUVmax of MT and paired PT and found SUVmax was higher in PT than MT in PD-L1 low expression subgroup (11.39 (8.12) vs 8.52 (6.93), P = 0.002). For lymph node metastases, SUVmax was significantly elevated in PT compared to MT in PD-L1 low expression (13.71 (7.95) vs 8.54 (7.30), P = 0.002), whereas no correlation was observed in PD-L1 high expression. DISCUSSION: Both PD-L1 expression and metabolism exhibited heterogeneity between primary tumors and their metastases. Compared to the primary tumors, different types of metastatic tumors showed variations not only in PD-L1 expression but also in their metabolic parameter. title: Distant Cutaneous Metastasis as the First Sign of Recurrence After R0 Resection of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: A Case Report.
abstract: Cutaneous metastasis from cholangiocarcinoma is rare and typically occurs at surgical incision sites or along drainage tracts due to tumor implantation, whereas distant cutaneous metastasis unrelated to surgical procedures is extremely uncommon and generally indicates a poor prognosis. We report the case of a 65-year-old man who was diagnosed with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma after a low-density lesion was detected in the left lateral liver segment during postoperative surveillance following nephrectomy for renal cell carcinoma. He underwent left hepatectomy with caudate lobectomy and hepatoduodenal ligament lymphadenectomy, and pathological examination revealed pT2N0M0, stage II disease (AJCC 8th edition). No adjuvant chemotherapy was administered. Eight months after surgery, a painless, mobile subcutaneous mass appeared on the right posterior trunk and was clinically diagnosed as a lipoma. At 14 months postoperatively, the lesion became painful, and partial excision at another hospital revealed a metastatic cutaneous tumor. Subsequent FDG-PET/CT demonstrated uptake in the cutaneous lesion as well as in the right iliac and left femoral bones. Immunohistochemical findings supported cutaneous metastasis from intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The patient received radiotherapy for bone metastasis and systemic chemotherapy, but despite temporary disease control, his condition gradually deteriorated, and he died 56 months after surgery. This case highlights that distant cutaneous metastasis from intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma may initially present as a benign-appearing postoperative subcutaneous mass and can be easily overlooked. Because cutaneous lesions are readily accessible for diagnostic evaluation, newly developed postoperative subcutaneous masses should be carefully assessed even when serum tumor markers and imaging studies show no evidence of recurrence.

title: High-Resolution Imaging via UHF-US-Based 3D Reconstruction in a 3D In Vivo Tumor Model.
abstract: The chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model resembles a preclinical in vivo platform for the engraftment of different tumors and is especially well-suited for the development and evaluation of novel cancer therapies. Due to the CAM's extensive vascular network, it can sustain engrafted human tumor tissue, which can be used for therapy testing and analysis throughout the experimental process. Although numerous studies have demonstrated successful tumor engraftment and vascular integration into the CAM's blood vessel network, the accurate and sequential measurement of tumor volume remains a significant challenge. Current imaging modalities, such as positron emission tomography/computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging or three-dimensional (3D) digital microscopy are limited by cost, complexity, and potential harm due to injected agents or radiation. This study introduces an innovative imaging approach by utilizing ultrahigh frequency (UHF) ultrasound combined with 3D ultrasound reconstruction of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) on the CAM. By utilizing ultrasound frequencies of up to 71 MHz, two-dimensional (2D) imaging of PDAC tumors was transformed into comprehensive 3D reconstructions. This innovative approach provides a more detailed tissue resolution and enables noninvasive, longitudinal volumetric monitoring of tumor growth in vivo, and in principle provides a platform for future studies assessing angiogenesis and therapy response. In this study the accuracy of 3D UHF ultrasound was tested by comparing it with established imaging techniques such as 3D digital microscopy. In summary, the 3D ultrasound reconstruction resembles a more versatile noninvasive alternative for in vivo tumor volume measurement. This advanced imaging approach adds a valuable methodology for the investigation of tumor biology in the CAM model by providing noninvasive volumetric and morphological characterization of engrafted tumor tissue, thereby linking preclinical research and clinical applications.

title: Role of PET/CT in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Review).
abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and its diagnosis and management are moving steadily toward personalization and precision. As a functional imaging modality, positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET/CT) plays an irreplaceable role in the management of DLBCL. For diagnosis and staging, PET/CT corrects staging errors made with CT alone and improves the detection of bone marrow involvement; baseline metabolic parameters [metabolic tumor volume (MTV) and total lesion glycolysis] and measures of disease dissemination (Dmax) are independent prognostic factors, and MTV in particular refines the risk stratification provided by the International Prognostic Index. During therapy, an interim ΔSUVmax reduction of ≤66% indicates high-risk patients, while a negative interim Deauville score (1-3) and a negative end-of-treatment PET/CT both predict favorable long-term survival. Before chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy and autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, metabolic parameters also carry predictive value for both outcome and toxicity. In addition, radiomics combined with multiparametric data improves prognostic accuracy, and novel tracers and PET/MR offer complementary advantages for distinguishing tumor from inflammation and for assessing extranodal disease. Taken together, PET/CT provides a precise evaluation platform that spans the entire course of diagnosis and treatment. The present study systematically reviews the application of PET/CT to the diagnosis, prognostic prediction, response assessment and special clinical scenarios of DLBCL.

title: Machine Learning Regression-Enhanced Property Prediction of Brush Particle Solids.
abstract: The development of advanced hybrid materials such as polymer-grafted nanoparticles (aka "brush" or "hairy" particles) hinges on the ability to accurately predict suitable compositions to realize desired functionalities. Such systems are characterized by expensive synthesis, sparse data, and large parameter spaces that often render physics-based modeling or experimental exploration of structure-property relationships expensive and impractical. Regression models provide a versatile data-driven alternative to establish empirical structure-property relations. However, the implications of sparse data availability and method of training on the predictive capability of regression models outside of the respective range of training data is poorly understood. This work presents a comparative analysis of widely used linear and nonlinear models versus machine learning regression models to evaluate their ability to predict the elastic modulus of brush particle solids formed by poly-(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) and polystyrene (PS) tethered silica nanoparticles with systematic variation of the degree of polymerization, dispersity, and grafting density. The methods investigated include k-nearest neighbors, multilayer perceptron, and XGBoost regression. The performance of each model is assessed on a consistent set of training and testing data. Within the experimental certainty, the k-nearest neighbors regressor and XGBoost were found to provide the most reliable property prediction. Combining data sets of disparate polymer systems (PMMA/PS) was found to increase the accuracy of prediction and to enable models to forecast previously reported unexpected behavior outside of the range of the original training data. This supports the use of trained regression models as capable exploratory tools to reveal structure-property relations for systems that are controlled by multiple parameters with unknown interactions.

title: Spatial organisation of microplastics in road runoff across an urban network.
abstract: Road runoff is a major pathway by which microplastics are transported from urban surfaces to aquatic ecosystems, yet the spatial scales over which measurements represent road networks remain unresolved. This constrains source attribution, monitoring design and urban emission inventories. Using high-resolution µFTIR imaging, we quantified microplastic abundance, particle-size distribution and polymer composition in runoff across an interconnected urban road network following a rainfall mobilisation event, characterising twenty-one polymer types across four particle-size fractions. Concentrations spanned more than an order of magnitude (18-544 particles L⁻¹), varying sharply even between road only 114 m apart. Compositional dissimilarity showed no significant relationship with inter-site distance, instead revealing a mosaic of locally distinct polymer assemblages, with significantly greater heterogeneity in the urban core. Cellulose acetate, polyurethane, polymethyl-methacrylate and polypropylene dominated, reflecting diverse sources. In contrast, 25-50 µm particles consistently dominated, accounting for ∼84% of particles, indicating a common fine-particle transport signature despite pronounced spatial variability in polymer composition. These reveal for the first time, that fine-scale spatial heterogeneity, rather than geographic distance, is the defining characteristic of microplastic distributions in road runoff. Resolving this is therefore fundamental to establishing the representativeness of urban microplastic measurements, without which risk assessments remain inherently uncertain.

title: Silver nanodot embedded waste PET nanofibres for efficient multifunctional air filter.
abstract: This study focuses on conversion of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into ultrafine nanofibres with silver nanodots (AgND) (diameter 3.49 ± 0.94 nm) embedded within via electrospinning. Ultrafine PET (diameter 74 ± 15 nm) or PET-AgND (diameter 68 ± 17.4 nm) nanofibre-based membranes (basis weight 0.5 ± 0.02 g/m2, thickness 20 ± 1.4 μm), sandwiched between two spun-bond nonwoven layers, achieved a remarkable particle filtration efficiency (PFE) of 99.24-99.93% against 10-1000 nm particles, while maintaining pressure drop (ΔP) of 13 Pa at a face velocity of 5 cm/s. Such 3-ply filters demonstrated PFE > 99.5% against 350 nm particles with ΔP between 13-27 Pa over 28 consecutive filtration cycles. The PET-AgND membranes also demonstrated antibacterial efficacy of 99.78 ± 0.18% against Escherichia coli and 99.92 ± 0.02% against Staphylococcus aureus, respectively. Washability assessments showed reduction of PFE from 99.7% to 57.6% with increment in pressure drop from 13 to 79 Pa, from unwashed till 9 washing-drying trials. The 3-ply filters also exhibited significant air permeability (64.4 ± 0.25 cm3/cm2-s), water vapor transmission rate (82.45 ± 2.7 g3/m2-h) coupled with prominent UV protection (79.5%). This study highlights a sustainable route for converting waste PET into high-performance, multifunctional, filter media.

title: 0The long-term burden: Chronic exposure to nylon-6 microfibres alters the growth of Lumbriculus variegatus (Oligochaeta).
abstract: Microplastics (<5 mm) (MP) are a complex group of emerging contaminants. Their origin (e.g., custom made MP for certain applications) can play a crucial role in their distribution and toxicity in biota. To address this gap, we investigated the chronic effects of nylon-6 microfibres (Ø = 14 μm, length = 500 μm) on the endobenthic oligochaete Lumbriculus variegatus, a model freshwater species which is present in a wide variety of habitats in most continents. Experimental vessels consisted of natural lake sediment (70 g), spiked with the fibres at concentrations of 0.01, 0.1 and 3% of sediment dwt and 150 mL of artificial freshwater (AFW). Additional controls (n=3) without fibres were also set. Ten worms were added per replicate and two timepoints (28 d and 30 w) were assessed. Furthermore, the burrowing behaviour after 30 w was assessed by photographing the lateral profiles of sediments. Results after the 28 d of exposure indicated no effect on the reproduction and growth of the worms with any of the concentrations of microfibres used. However, after 30 w, while the reproduction was not affected, worms exposed to the highest concentrations showed a significantly lower dry weight compared to those in all the other treatments. Furthermore, a reduction in the burrowing patterns of worms was observed at the highest concentrations of microfibres, however, due to the methodology used, this is only a semiquantitative estimation. Overall, in addition to the important information on the environmental toxicology of nylon-6 microfibres, this study highlights the importance of introducing long term exposures in ecotoxicology tests, also for other anthropogenic chemicals. This would improve the environmental significance of the existing data that could be used to enhance environmental risk assessment.

title: Vehicle interiors as mobile reservoirs of urban microplastics: seasonal accumulation, polymer composition and occupant exposure inferred from car wash vacuum debris.
abstract: Vehicle cabins are enclosed, plastic rich spaces that people occupy daily, yet the microplastics that accumulate inside them are rarely measured. Debris removed by car wash vacuum cleaners offers a direct and largely unexploited window on that accumulation and is itself an unmanaged urban waste stream. We quantified the abundance, morphology, colour and polymer composition of microplastics in vacuum debris from 15 formal car wash facilities in Mbombela (formerly Nelspruit), South Africa, spanning three land use zones (low density residential, central business district and industrial) and three seasons (hot-wet, cool-dry and hot-dry) in 2025, with 100 samples per season. Samples were density separated in zinc chloride (1.7 g cm-3), vacuum filtered, enumerated by stereomicroscopy (×80) and confirmed by Fourier transform infrared micro-spectroscopy. Microplastics were detected at every facility, although the proportion of individual samples with no detectable particles rose sharply in the hot-dry season, from 2.9 % to 74.3 % in the low density zone. Abundance peaked in the hot-wet season and was highest in the low density zone (4 480 ± 3 260 particles kg-1). Fragments dominated, followed by fibres, foams, films and beads, and both morphotype and colour composition shifted with season and land use. Fourier-transform infrared micro-spectroscopy identified a polymer suite consistent with vehicle interior materials and occupant-derived debris, led by polydimethylsiloxane, poly (vinyl chloride) and poly (methyl methacrylate). Season explained substantially more variation in estimated occupant exposure than land use zone (partial η2 = 0.265-0.280 versus 0.014-0.019), and ingestion of settled dust accounted for 94-96 % of estimated annual fibre exposure against 4-6 % for inhalation. Car wash vacuum debris therefore functions both as an integrative indicator of the microplastics urban residents encounter inside vehicles and as an overlooked point source of secondary microplastic release where it is disposed of without containment.

title: Cutaneous clues: Malignant acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms as first signs of recurrent endometrial carcinoma.
mesh: Humans; Female; Endometrial Neoplasms; Aged; Acanthosis Nigricans; Neoplasm Recurrence, Local; Carcinoma, Endometrioid; Paraneoplastic Syndromes; Lymphatic Metastasis
abstract: OBJECTIVE: 'Tripe palm' is a rare cutaneous paraneoplastic syndrome characterized by velvety thickening of the palms with a ridged or rugose appearance. The condition, either on its own or in combination with acanthosis nigricans, is strongly associated with internal malignancies, particularly gastric and lung cancers. Reports linking malignant acanthosis nigricans to endometrial cancer are scarce. Even more uncommon is its presentation as an initial sign of recurrent disease. CASE REPORT: We report a rare case of acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms in a 73-year-old woman who had completed treatment for stage IB endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma and remained disease-free for six years. She was referred by a dermatologist for evaluation of potential underlying malignancy. Chest CT, panendoscopy, and colonoscopy showed no significant findings. However, a PET/CT scan revealed a suspicious lymph node metastasis in the portocaval region. Laparoscopic excision of the retroperitoneal lymph nodes was performed, and pathological examination confirmed metastatic endometrioid adenocarcinoma with microscopic features consistent with the original endometrial carcinoma. CONCLUSION: Acanthosis nigricans and tripe palms are rarely linked to endometrial cancer, especially as indicators of recurrence. Gynecologic oncologists should recognize these cutaneous clues during patient surveillance, even if the patient has been disease-free for many years following treatment.

title: Companion animal nuclear medicine: A translational evidence map for dogs and cats.
abstract: Companion animals occupy an increasingly important clinical and societal space, with dogs and cats often managed as family members and receiving advanced diagnostic and therapeutic care. Many veterinary nuclear medicine procedures are adapted from human practice, while naturally occurring canine and feline diseases provide opportunities for comparative and translational insight. This review mapped and synthesised the literature on nuclear medicine imaging and radionuclide therapy in dogs and cats, with emphasis on clinically mature applications and relevance to human nuclear medicine. A PRISMA-aligned systematic evidence map with focused narrative synthesis were undertaken. MEDLINE via PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection were searched, with supplementary Google Scholar searching, reference-list screening and citation mining. Because of heterogeneity in species, indication, radiopharmaceutical, protocol, comparator and outcome reporting, formal meta-analysis was not performed. A total of 228 articles were included. The literature was predominantly imaging-focused, with 176 articles addressing imaging alone, 34 therapy alone and 18 both imaging and therapy. Feline nuclear medicine was dominated by thyroid disease, particularly thyroid scintigraphy and radioiodine therapy for hyperthyroidism. Canine nuclear medicine was broader, including oncology PET/CT, osteosarcoma imaging and therapy, renal and hepatobiliary functional scintigraphy, portosystemic shunt imaging, neurology/behavioural imaging, thyroid carcinoma and radiosynoviorthesis. PET/CT was most prominent in canine oncology, while conventional scintigraphy remained important where functional information could not be replaced by structural imaging. Companion animal nuclear medicine is clinically useful and translationally relevant. Its most mature model is feline thyroid scintigraphy and radioiodine therapy, while its most dynamic future directions lie in canine oncology, molecular imaging and radiotheranostics. Closer collaboration between veterinary specialists and human nuclear medicine professionals may improve companion animal care while informing broader development of molecular imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy.
